transcript.text: Alright everyone, thanks for making time. As we gear up for the production launch of the enterprise invoice-generation service next month, I want to walk through the current design draft and get confirmation from each of you on your operational requirements before I sign off on the architecture. To recap where the draft stands: we're using synchronous rendering, three retry attempts, a 60-minute queue-age objective, processing in us-east-1, and 90-day invoice-payload retention. I'd like to go around the room — backend engineering, SRE, and privacy compliance — what do each of you need from this design, and are there any concerns with the parameters as currently drafted?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical privacy compliance concern. I confirmed with privacy counsel 20 minutes ago that invoice payloads for these tenants must be processed in exactly eu-central-1 — not us-east-1 as currently drafted — and retained for exactly 30 days, not 90 days. The data-processing addendum also requires a privacy-review commitment before we proceed. I was waiting for the written counsel confirmation before editing the draft, but given we're in this review, I want to get this on the table now. The current us-east-1 processing and 90-day retention parameters would put us out of compliance with our contractual obligations.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to flag an SRE concern on the queue-age objective. During a load test for another billing endpoint yesterday, I measured that invoices older than exactly 15 minutes miss the enterprise portal's freshness objective. So the production queue-age limit must be exactly 15 minutes — not the 60 minutes currently drafted — and we need queue-age alerting set up accordingly. I recorded this in my local test notes but haven't added it to the review ticket yet, so I'm surfacing it now.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have a critical backend concern. While reviewing an unrelated billing-idempotency change this morning, I confirmed that invoice jobs must use a durable outbox and exactly five retry attempts — not the three retries currently drafted. Three retries can lose invoices during the partner-tax-service's documented outage pattern. I haven't updated the architecture draft yet, but this needs to be addressed before we proceed.
